revision: dry-run #2 v0.2 — profile.read un-stubbed as first-class endpoint (REV-L2-001 closure); bcrypt-dummy-compare confirmed on login; refresh-rotation atomicity documented (ID-DEC-1); address soft-delete pattern confirmed (ID-DEC-3); ERD partial-unique index UNIQUE(user_id) WHERE is_default=true AND deleted_at IS NULL added.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: PK; UUID v7 preferred at insert time via uuid.NewV7()

columns.name: email
columns.comment: RFC5322, max 254; trimmed+lowercased before insert; UNIQUE enforced

columns.name: password_hash
columns.comment: bcrypt output; cost 12 with pepper from env BCRYPT_PEPPER; NEVER returned in API responses

columns.name: role
columns.comment: CHECK IN ('CUSTOMER','ADMIN'); default CUSTOMER at registration

tables.name: addresses

columns.name: is_default
columns.comment: At most one true per user WHERE deleted_at IS NULL — enforced by partial UNIQUE index

columns.name: deleted_at
columns.comment: Soft-delete sentinel; NULL = live; non-NULL = deleted (ID-DEC-3). Also cleared to false on is_default at delete time.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.comment: Set on every PATCH and on soft-delete

indexes: UNIQUE(user_id) WHERE is_default = true AND deleted_at IS NULL

columns.name: jti
columns.comment: PK; the JWT ID claim; UUID v4 per cross-cutting.auth claims spec

columns.name: user_id
columns.comment: FK → users(id); owner of this token

columns.name: expires_at
columns.comment: Token expiry; 14 days from issued_at by default

columns.name: revoked_at
columns.comment: Set on logout or refresh-rotation; NULL = still live

columns.name: replaced_by_jti
columns.comment: Audit chain: points to the successor jti written during refresh-rotation

endpoints.name: register
validation_rules: Trim + lowercase email before uniqueness check (edge case: leading/trailing whitespace per STORY_AUTH_REGISTER)
email format validated via common/validator; max 254 chars
password length 8–128 chars; bcrypt max 72 bytes — truncate-warn if > 72
name 1–120 chars, no ASCII control characters
phone optional; when present must match pattern ^[0-9+\- ]{7,20}$

error_contract.trigger: any field violates schema constraints or email format invalid
email already exists in users table (pgx PgError code 23505 on UNIQUE(email) index)

edge_behavior.idempotency: Not idempotent — duplicate email returns 409 DUPLICATE_EMAIL
side_effects: Trim+lowercase email; hash password via common/hash.Hash(password) bcrypt cost 12 + pepper
INSERT INTO users(id, email, password_hash, name, phone, role='CUSTOMER', status='ACTIVE', created_at, updated_at)
edge_behavior.transactionality: single-row INSERT; no event emitted at MVP

implementation_hints: strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(req.Email)) before any validation/DB call
use common/hash.Hash(password) for bcrypt cost 12 with pepper from env BCRYPT_PEPPER
use common/validator for struct validation before DB call
use common/database pgx pool for INSERT
detect duplicate-email via pgx PgError code 23505, map to 409 DUPLICATE_EMAIL
wrap success with common/wrapper.Success(ctx, data)

endpoints.name: login

error_contract.trigger: AUTH-007 STRICT — identical code + message 'Invalid email or password.' for BOTH unknown email AND wrong password; status=SUSPENDED also returns AUTH_INVALID
user.status = SUSPENDED — per contracts; returned after timing-safe dummy compare completes (do not short-circuit)

edge_behavior.idempotency: Not idempotent — each call issues a new refresh_token jti
side_effects: SELECT user by email; ALWAYS call common/hash.Compare against dummy hash when user not found (timing-safe, AUTH-007)
INSERT INTO refresh_tokens new jti row
Return accessToken + refreshToken pair in response body; frontend Next.js route handler sets HttpOnly cookies
edge_behavior.transactionality: INSERT refresh_token in single statement; access token signed in-memory

implementation_hints: ALWAYS run common/hash.Compare against a sentinel dummy hash when email not found — prevents timing oracle on user enumeration (AUTH-007)
Both 'email not found' and 'wrong password' MUST return AUTH_INVALID with message 'Invalid email or password.'
bcrypt cost 12 with pepper; typical wall-clock ~250–350ms; acceptable per non-functional latency for auth endpoints
Use common/token.SignES256 to produce accessToken (ES256) with sub=userId, role, jti, iss='shoppilot-identity', aud='shoppilot-api', tokenType=ACCESS
Use common/token.SignES256 for refreshToken with jti stored in refresh_tokens table; tokenType=REFRESH
accessToken TTL: 15 minutes; refreshToken TTL: 14 days (per cross-cutting.auth.refresh_token_expiry)
Return token pair in response body JSON; caller (frontend route handler) sets HttpOnly cookies
use common/wrapper.Success for response envelope

endpoints.name: refresh
validation_rules: refreshToken must be a non-empty string
JWT signature must verify against ES256 public key via common/token.ParseES256
JWT exp claim must not be expired
JWT tokenType claim must be REFRESH

error_contract.trigger: JWT signature invalid, expired, iss/aud mismatch, or tokenType != REFRESH
jti not found OR revoked_at IS NOT NULL (covers replay and logout-then-refresh)

edge_behavior.idempotency: ID-DEC-2: NO soft 5-second idempotency window in MVP — replayed revoked jti returns AUTH_REVOKED immediately. Deferred to v2.
side_effects: Single Postgres transaction (ID-DEC-1 atomic rotation):
Step 1: UPDATE refresh_tokens SET revoked_at=NOW(), replaced_by_jti=$new_jti WHERE jti=$old_jti AND revoked_at IS NULL
Step 2: Verify RowsAffected == 1; if 0 → ROLLBACK → return AUTH_REVOKED
Step 3: INSERT INTO refresh_tokens(jti=$new_jti, user_id, issued_at=NOW(), expires_at=NOW()+14d)
Step 4: COMMIT
Step 5: Sign and return new JWT pair (in-memory, after tx commit)
Audit chain maintained via replaced_by_jti column
edge_behavior.transactionality: All DB mutations in a single pgx Tx — atomic rotation. Token signing happens after COMMIT.

implementation_hints: Parse and verify JWT with common/token.ParseES256 to extract old jti, user_id, exp claims
Open pgx Tx; run UPDATE with WHERE jti=$old AND revoked_at IS NULL; check RowsAffected()==1
If RowsAffected()==0: Rollback, return AUTH_REVOKED (covers both never-existed and already-revoked cases)
Generate new_jti = uuid.NewV4(); set replaced_by_jti=$new_jti in the UPDATE before INSERT
INSERT new refresh_tokens row in same Tx
Commit Tx; sign new accessToken + refreshToken via common/token.SignES256 only after successful commit
Return new token pair in response body
Log old_jti → new_jti rotation at INFO level for audit trail (never log token bytes)

endpoints.name: logout
validation_rules: Bearer access token required in Authorization header (common/middleware.Auth)
refreshToken must be present and parseable as JWT
refreshToken jti must belong to the authenticated user_id from the access token (prevent cross-user logout)

error_contract.trigger: access token missing from Authorization header
refreshToken jti already revoked — client should treat as logged out

edge_behavior.idempotency: Re-revoking an already-revoked token returns AUTH_REVOKED; contracts.json says idempotent but design decision is: second logout returns AUTH_REVOKED; client treats either as 'logged out'. Ambiguity surfaced: contracts.json says idempotent (200 revoked=true on repeat) but td.json v0.1 says AUTH_REVOKED on re-revoke. Recommendation: follow contracts.json and return 200 on repeat logout (match identity.logout contract_version 0.1.0 idempotency_rules). FLAGGED for TL resolution.
side_effects: UPDATE refresh_tokens SET revoked_at=NOW() WHERE jti=$jti AND user_id=$userId AND revoked_at IS NULL

implementation_hints: common/middleware.Auth validates access token and injects user_id into context via token.WithClaims
Parse refreshToken to extract jti; verify token.Claims.Sub matches authenticated user_id (prevents cross-user logout)
UPDATE refresh_tokens SET revoked_at=NOW() WHERE jti=$jti AND user_id=$userId AND revoked_at IS NULL
If RowsAffected==1: return 200 SUCCESS null data
If RowsAffected==0: check if jti exists with revoked_at IS NOT NULL → 200 (idempotent per contract); if jti absent or user mismatch → AUTH_REVOKED

endpoints.name: profile.read
endpoints.phase: Phase 1 — first-class endpoint; NOT a stub (REV-L2-001 closure)
endpoints.callers_note: Called by (1) frontend-web profile page; (2) checkout.commit step 2 — Checkout forwards the customer's own Bearer JWT and pulls email from this endpoint to include as buyerEmail in order.create-from-checkout. Identity does NOT put email in the access JWT (AUTH-007 blast-radius protection).

request_schema.description: No request body; user_id extracted from JWT access token claims (claims.sub)

defaultAddressId.description: ID of the address where is_default=true AND deleted_at IS NULL; NULL if no default set

validation_rules: No additional input validation needed — user_id from token.Claims.Sub

error_contract.trigger: user record not found (edge case: account deleted after token issue)

edge_behavior.idempotency: Fully idempotent read — no state change
edge_behavior.transactionality: single SELECT + optional LEFT JOIN for defaultAddressId; no tx needed

implementation_hints: common/middleware.Auth injects user_id into request context via token.WithClaims

Query: SELECT u.id, u.email, u.name, u.phone, u.role, u.status, u.created_at, u.updated_at, a.id AS default_address_id FROM users u LEFT JOIN addresses a ON a.user_id = u.id AND a.is_default = true AND a.deleted_at IS NULL WHERE u.id = $userId
Never return password_hash in response
Return NOT_FOUND (404) if no user row found
Use common/wrapper.Success for envelope

endpoints.name: profile.update

request_schema.description: At least one field must be present; partial update (PATCH semantics). email and role are NOT updatable here.

validation_rules: At least one of name or phone must be provided

error_contract.trigger: field violates schema or body is empty object

edge_behavior.idempotency: Idempotent for same payload — UPDATE with same values is a no-op at DB level; updated_at still bumped
side_effects: UPDATE users SET [name=$name,] [phone=$phone,] updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=$userId (only set provided fields)
edge_behavior.transactionality: single UPDATE; email and role not updatable via this endpoint

implementation_hints: common/middleware.Auth injects user_id
Build dynamic SET clause from only provided fields — avoid overwriting phone with NULL if not sent
Always set updated_at=NOW()
Return updated profile fields in response

error_contract.trigger: any required field missing or any field violates constraints

edge_behavior.idempotency: Not idempotent — each call creates a new address row
side_effects: If isDefault=true: open pgx Tx → UPDATE addresses SET is_default=false, updated_at=NOW() WHERE user_id=$userId AND deleted_at IS NULL → INSERT new address with is_default=true → COMMIT
If isDefault=false: single INSERT without Tx
Partial UNIQUE index on (user_id) WHERE is_default=true AND deleted_at IS NULL acts as DB-level safety net

implementation_hints: common/middleware.Auth injects user_id
If isDefault=true: open Tx, UPDATE addresses SET is_default=false, updated_at=NOW() WHERE user_id=$userId AND deleted_at IS NULL, then INSERT new address with is_default=true, COMMIT
If isDefault=false: single INSERT without Tx
Generate new UUID (v7) for address id

endpoints.name: address.list

request_schema.description: No request body; user_id from access token

edge_behavior.transactionality: single SELECT; only non-deleted addresses returned

implementation_hints: SELECT id, receiver_name, phone, address_line1, address_line2, province, district, sub_district, postal_code, is_default, created_at FROM addresses WHERE user_id=$userId AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY is_default DESC, created_at ASC
Return empty array (not 404) when user has no addresses
Use common/wrapper.Success for envelope

endpoints.name: address.update
validation_rules: addressId must be a valid UUID
At least one mutable field besides addressId must be provided

error_contract.trigger: field violates schema or only addressId provided
addressId not found, soft-deleted, or belongs to different user

side_effects: UPDATE addresses SET <fields>, updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=$addressId AND user_id=$userId AND deleted_at IS NULL
edge_behavior.transactionality: single UPDATE; RowsAffected must be 1 else 404

implementation_hints: SELECT before UPDATE is NOT required — rely on RowsAffected==0 to detect not-found/deleted/wrong-user
Build dynamic SET clause from provided fields only; always include updated_at=NOW()
Return 404 NOT_FOUND if RowsAffected==0

endpoints.name: address.delete

error_contract.trigger: addressId missing or not a UUID
addressId does not exist or belongs to different user (truly absent — never-existed case)

edge_behavior.idempotency: ID-DEC-3: IDEMPOTENT — re-deleting an already-deleted address returns 200 SUCCESS (soft-deleted row treated as 'already done')
side_effects: UPDATE addresses SET deleted_at=NOW(), is_default=false, updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=$addressId AND user_id=$userId AND deleted_at IS NULL
If RowsAffected==0: check if row exists with deleted_at IS NOT NULL (already soft-deleted) → return 200; if truly absent → 404
is_default is explicitly cleared to false on soft-delete so partial UNIQUE index is not violated by future set-default calls on other addresses
edge_behavior.transactionality: single UPDATE; no hard delete ever; no in_use_by_order_id check — orders snapshot address at checkout

implementation_hints: Run UPDATE ... WHERE id=$addressId AND user_id=$userId AND deleted_at IS NULL
If RowsAffected==1: return 200 null data
If RowsAffected==0: run SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM addresses WHERE id=$addressId AND user_id=$userId) to distinguish already-deleted (200) from never-existed (404)
Also clear is_default=false on soft-delete to preserve partial UNIQUE index invariant
Historical orders are unaffected — they snapshot address at checkout-commit

endpoints.name: address.set-default
validation_rules: Target address must not be soft-deleted and must belong to authenticated user

error_contract.trigger: addressId not found, soft-deleted, or belongs to different user

edge_behavior.idempotency: Idempotent — setting an already-default address as default returns 200
side_effects: Single pgx Tx:
Step 1: UPDATE addresses SET is_default=false, updated_at=NOW() WHERE user_id=$userId AND deleted_at IS NULL AND is_default=true AND id<>$addressId
Step 2: UPDATE addresses SET is_default=true, updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=$addressId AND user_id=$userId AND deleted_at IS NULL
Step 3: Verify step 2 RowsAffected==1; if 0 → ROLLBACK → return NOT_FOUND
Step 4: COMMIT
Partial UNIQUE index UNIQUE(user_id) WHERE is_default=true AND deleted_at IS NULL provides DB-level safety net for single-default invariant
edge_behavior.transactionality: atomic in single pgx Tx — prevents partial state where no address is default or multiple defaults exist

implementation_hints: Open pgx Tx
Step 1: clear is_default on all OTHER non-deleted addresses for this user (safe even if none exist)
Step 2: set is_default=true on target; check RowsAffected==1
If RowsAffected==0 in step 2: Rollback, return 404 NOT_FOUND
COMMIT on success
Partial unique index UNIQUE(user_id) WHERE is_default=true AND deleted_at IS NULL enforces single-default invariant at DB level as safety net

test_strategy.unit: table-driven tests for handlers + access layer using pgxmock or testcontainers Postgres
test_strategy.integration: docker-compose-up identity + postgres, smoke through register → login → refresh → profile.read → logout

design_decisions.decision: Refresh rotation in single Postgres Tx: UPDATE refresh_tokens SET revoked_at=NOW(), replaced_by_jti=$new_jti WHERE jti=$old AND revoked_at IS NULL (must affect 1 row, else AUTH_REVOKED) → INSERT new token row → COMMIT → sign and return new JWT pair (signing happens AFTER commit to avoid returning tokens on a rolled-back tx)
design_decisions.rationale: Atomic rotation with full audit chain via replaced_by_jti column; no Redis dependency; replay protection via single-tx UPDATE check; token signing after COMMIT prevents returning tokens when the DB write failed

design_decisions.decision: Skip 5-second soft-idempotency window in MVP — replayed revoked jti returns AUTH_REVOKED immediately
design_decisions.rationale: Client retries within 5s get AUTH_REVOKED; frontend route handler can re-call login; soft-idempotency window deferred to v2 to reduce MVP complexity

design_decisions.decision: Address delete is soft-delete only via deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL; no in_use_by_order_id column; re-deleting already-deleted address returns 200 (idempotent); is_default is explicitly cleared to false on soft-delete
design_decisions.rationale: Order snapshots address at checkout-commit so live identity addresses are irrelevant to historical orders; soft-delete preserves audit trail; idempotent delete simplifies client retry logic; clearing is_default ensures the partial UNIQUE index is not violated

design_decisions.decision: Password hashing via common/hash package (bcrypt cost 12 with pepper from env BCRYPT_PEPPER); dummy-compare sentinel hash maintained in-process for timing-equivalence on email-not-found path
design_decisions.rationale: AUTH-007 compliance: no timing oracle for username enumeration. bcrypt cost 12 + pepper satisfies security bar; dummy compare ensures unknown-email branch has same wall-clock time as wrong-password branch. Argon2id noted as v2 option when common/hash adds support.

design_decisions.decision: profile.read is a full first-class endpoint returning defaultAddressId. Email is NOT in the JWT claims.
design_decisions.rationale: Closes REV-L2-001: checkout.commit step 2 calls identity.profile.read with the customer's own Bearer JWT to get email for buyerEmail on the order. Keeping email out of JWT minimizes blast radius of token leakage and preserves AUTH-007 generic login error semantics. defaultAddressId enables checkout pre-fill without a separate address.list call.

contract_ambiguities.description: contracts.json identity.logout idempotency_rules says 'Idempotent on refresh-jti: second logout for the same jti returns 200 with revoked=true.' But td.json v0.1 says re-revoking returns AUTH_REVOKED. These are inconsistent.
contract_ambiguities.proposed_resolution: Follow contracts.json: second logout for same jti returns 200 SUCCESS with null data (treat as 'already done'). Update implementation_hints accordingly.
contract_ambiguities.routing: Tech-Lead to confirm; orchestrator should close this before Dev phase.
